title: 6–16 February: 53rd Berlin International Film Festival
text: The 53rd annual Berlin International Film Festival was held from February 6–16, 2003. The festival opened with musical film Chicago by Rob Marshall and closed with Martin Scorsese's Gangs of New York, both films played out of competition at the festival.

title: Germany in the Eurovision Song Contest 2003
text: Germany was represented at the Eurovision Song Contest 2003 with the song "Let's Get Happy", composed by Ralph Siegel, with lyrics by Bernd Meinunger, and performed by Louise Hoffner, more commonly referred to as Lou. The German participating broadcaster on behalf of ARD, Norddeutscher Rundfunk, organised the national final Countdown Grand Prix Eurovision 2003 in order to select their entry for the contest.
wiki: Germany in the Eurovision Song Contest 2003

title: Death of Jeremiah Duggan
text: Jeremiah Joseph Duggan was a British student in Paris who died during a visit to Wiesbaden, Hesse, Germany, after being struck by several motorists on a dual carriageway. The circumstances of Duggan's death became a matter of dispute because, at the time he died, he was attending a youth "cadre" school organised by the LaRouche movement, an international network led by the American political activist Lyndon LaRouche.

title: Accident on the Bundesautobahn 5
text: The accident on the Bundesautobahn 5 occurred on 14 July 2003 close to Karlsruhe, Germany, when a young mother lost control of her car on Bundesautobahn 5 and collided with a tree. The 21-year-old woman and her two-year-old daughter died at the scene.

title: Learning Resource Server Medicine is developed in German and English for medicine and dentistry learning and teaching.
text: The Learning Resource Server Medicine is a free-to-access catalog of electronic learning and teaching software modules for education in medicine and dentistry available in English and German.

title: 2003 Men's European Volleyball Championship
text: The 2003 Men's European Volleyball Championship was the 23rd edition of the event, organized by Europe's governing volleyball body, the Confédération Européenne de Volleyball. It was hosted in Berlin, Germany from September 5 to September 14, 2003.

title: 2002–03 Deutsche Eishockey Liga season
text: The 2002–03 Deutsche Eishockey Liga season was the 9th season since the founding of the Deutsche Eishockey Liga. The Krefeld Pinguine became German Champions.

title: 2003 German motorcycle Grand Prix
text: The 2003 German motorcycle Grand Prix was the ninth round of the 2003 MotoGP Championship. It took place on the weekend of 25–27 July 2003 at the Sachsenring.

title: “Der Steuersong” by Die Gerd-Show
text: "The Ketchup Song" (Andalusian pronunciation: ) is a song by Spanish pop group Las Ketchup, released as the lead single from their debut studio album, Hijas del Tomate (2002). The song is about a young man who enters a nightclub while singing and dancing.

title: “We Have a Dream” by Deutschland sucht den Superstar
text: "We Have a Dream" is a song from the first series of German reality talent show Deutschland sucht den Superstar. Written and produced by contest judge Dieter Bohlen, the song is performed by the first series' final 10 contestants, who were credited by the programme's name for the single release.

title: “All the Things She Said” by t.A.T.u.
text: "All the Things She Said" is a song by Russian music duo t.A.T.u. from their first English-language studio album, 200 km/h in the Wrong Lane.
listen: All the Things She Said t.A.T.u.

title: “Take Me Tonight” by 31 March
text: "Take Me Tonight" is a song by German recording artist Alexander Klaws, the winner of the inaugural season of the television competition Deutschland sucht den Superstar. Written and produced by DSDS judge Dieter Bohlen, it was released as both his coronation song and debut single.

title: “No Angel (It's All in Your Mind)” by No Angels
text: "No Angel" is a song by German pop band No Angels. It was written by Pete Kirtley, Tim Hawes and Liz Winstanley for the group's third studio album, Pure (2003), while production was helmed by Nik Hafemann along with Arno Kammermeier, Peter Hayo, and Walter Merziger who are credited under their production moniker Perky Park.

title: “In da Club” by 50 Cent
text: "In da Club" is a song by American rapper 50 Cent from his debut studio album Get Rich or Die Tryin'. Written by 50 Cent alongside producers Dr.

title: “Für dich” by Yvonne Catterfeld
text: "Für dich" is a song by German singer Yvonne Catterfeld. It was written by Dieter Bohlen, Klaus Hirschburger and Lukas Hilbert and the produced by the former for her debut studio album, Meine Welt (2003).

title: “Aicha” by 7 July
text: Aïcha "Aïcha" is a song written by French singer-songwriter Jean-Jacques Goldman, performed by Algerian raï artist Khaled. In 1996, the song was released as a single containing two versions: a French version and a bilingual version sung in both French and Arabic.

title: “In the Shadows” by 11 August
text: "In the Shadows" is a song by Finnish alternative rock band the Rasmus, included on the group's fifth studio album, Dead Letters. Released in Finland in January 2003, the single achieved considerable chart success throughout Europe and Oceania, topping the charts of Finland, Germany, Hungary, and New Zealand and peaking at No.

title: “Ich denk an dich” by Pur
text: Pur is a German pop band from Bietigheim-Bissingen.

title: “Burger Dance” by DJ Ötzi featuring Eric Dikeb
text: "Fast Food Song" is a song made famous by British-based band Fast Food Rockers, although it existed long before they recorded it, as a popular children's playground song. The chorus is based on the Moroccan folk tune "A Ram Sam Sam" and mentions fast food restaurant chains McDonald's, Kentucky Fried Chicken and Pizza Hut.

title: “Never Leave You (Uh Oooh, Uh Oooh)” by Lumidee featuring Busta Rhymes and Fabolous
text: "Never Leave You" is a song by American recording artist Lumidee, released as her debut single on May 12, 2003, from her first album, Almost Famous (2003). The song features a sample from Diwali Riddim by Lenky, released in 2002.

title: “Angel of Berlin” by Martin Kesici
text: Martin Kesici is a German singer-songwriter and television personality. Kesici rose to prominence after winning the German version of Star Search, a popular US talent contest.

title: “Unrockbar” by 29 September
text: "Unrockbar" is a punk song by German band Die Ärzte. It's the first track on CD2 and the first single from their 2003 album Geräusch.

title: “White Flag” by Dido
text: "White Flag" is a song by English singer-songwriter Dido, released as the lead single from her second studio album, Life for Rent. The song was first released to US radio on 7 July 2003 and was issued in the United Kingdom as a physical single on 1 September 2003.

title: “Where Is the Love?” by The Black Eyed Peas
text: "Where Is the Love?" is a song by American hip hop group the Black Eyed Peas. It was released on May 12, 2003, as the lead single from their third album, Elephunk.
listen: Where Is the Love? The Black Eyed Peas

title: “Free Like the Wind” by Alexander
text: "Free Like the Wind" is a song by German recording artist Alexander Klaws. Written and produced by frequent contributor Dieter Bohlen, it was released as the lead single from Klaws's second album Here I Am, while serving as the theme song for the television film Hero of the Gladiators (2003).

title: “Schick mir 'nen Engel” by Overground
text: "Schick mir 'nen Engel" is a song by German boy band Overground. Composed by the Triple–M collective, it was written by Mike Michaels, MM Dollar, Sammy Naja, O.K.A.N., and TK-Roxx and produced by Michaels, Dollar, Mark Tabak, and Naja for their debut studio album It's Done (2003).

title: “Everyday Girl” by Preluders
text: "Everyday Girl" is a song by German girl group Preluders. It was written by Fredrik Björk and Per Eklund and produced by Jörn-Uwe Fahrenkrog-Petersen and Gena Wernik for their debut studio album, Girls in the House.

title: “Music Is the Key” by 15 December
text: "Music Is the Key" is a song by German recording artist Sarah Connor and all-male American a cappella group Naturally 7. The song was written and produced by longtime collaborators Rob Tyger and Kay Denar and recorded for Connor's third studio album, Key to My Soul.
